subject: On-site Kubernetes: zoning, JBOD -> Block fallback & storage/Nodeclass constraints
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-11T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: On-site Kubernetes: zoning, JBOD -> Block fallback & storage/Nodeclass constraints

Samir —

Thanks for the intake call earlier. To keep the preflight focused, here are the things we need to lock down for the on-site private cluster runbook and to produce the final deployment BOM:

1) Fault domains & control plane topology
   - Desired control-plane replicas (we recommend 3 across separate racks/subnets).
   - Confirmation whether the site has 2 or 3 independent rack-level failure domains.

2) Node classes & sizing (high level)
   - Inference nodes: GPU nodepool(s) with local NVMe for model cache (we typically recommend 2 NVMe per GPU node, 1.5-2TB each, for hot KV/cache).
   - Stateful blockstore nodes: either customer SAN or clustered block store (Ceph/Rook or Longhorn). Need to know whether you want local JBOD per rack or an external iSCSI SAN.
   - Control/infra nodes: 3 x m (CPU, 32-64GB) with stable storage for etcd snapshots.

3) Storage expectations and fallback behavior
   - RPO/RTO for model artifacts and inference logs (e.g., logs acceptable to lose up to 30s of KV cache vs. models must be durable).
   - If we cannot guarantee cross-rack persistent replication (JBOD-only), Redwood will configure a local NVMe model cache + a fallback path to block storage (iSCSI or SAN) for durable artifacts. We need to know permitted cross-rack traffic for replication.

4) Network & egress restrictions
   - Are egress rules limited to a managed NAT or is no external egress allowed for worker nodes?
   - Customer-managed KMS (Vault/HSM) details if encryption keys are external.

5) Security/compliance points
   - Required audit log retention window and whether logs must leave the site.
   - Any required host-level hardening baseline (CIS profile, approved OS image).

Action items for you: share the site rack count, whether there is SAN (iSCSI/Fibre) or only local JBOD, and the KMS details.

I attached a quick diagram of the suggested zoning and fallback paths. If you prefer, we can sketch an alternative that uses on-site Ceph/Rook for replication vs. SAN-backed volumes.

Cheers,
Laura
Director, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: On-site Kubernetes: zoning, JBOD -> Block fallback & storage/Nodeclass constraints

Laura / team —

Thanks — quick answers below to unblock your BOM:

- Rack topology: 2 racks in the primary datacenter room. Each rack has dual top-of-rack switches. We do not have a third rack in the same fault domain.
- SAN: We have a legacy SAN (iSCSI) connected to both racks via redundant FC-iSCSI gateways. Storage team prefers SAN for durable volumes; however, SAN perf for small random IO is variable.
- Local JBOD: Each rack also has 4 JBOD chassis (NVMe + SATA) available for ephemeral/cache uses.
- KMS: We run HashiCorp Vault (HA) in our VMs; we can provide a customer-managed KMS endpoint. No external HSM.
- Egress: Worker nodes cannot initiate outbound traffic to the public internet except via a customer-controlled NAT gateway (we can white-list Redwood control plane IPs if needed).
- RPO for models: models must be durable within 10 minutes (fastest approach is to push to SAN after successful deploy); KV cache can be ephemeral.
- GPUs: We have 4 x A100 nodes available initially (2 per rack). Expected steady inference QPS ~250 calls/sec with bursts to 600 for a few hours/day.

Attached network map and a short note from our storage team on current SAN volumes.

Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Platform Engineering — Novamed

Subject: Re: On-site Kubernetes: zoning, JBOD -> Block fallback & storage/Nodeclass constraints

Folks —

Thanks Samir — useful context. A few recommendations and constraints from our side to keep the deployment within SLA and security controls:

1) Control plane placement
   - With 2 rack fault domains we should place 3 control-plane nodes with etcd voting across both racks plus a lightweight tie-breaker (a small VM in an adjacent management VLAN or a third neutral facility if available). Running 3 control-plane nodes across only 2 racks is acceptable but we need to be explicit about the impact of a full-rack outage.

2) Storage pattern (recommended path)
   - For durable model artifacts: prefer SAN-backed PVs exposed via the customer iSCSI SAN (multipath) for durability and easier snapshotting under your storage team.
   - For model cache and inference KV: use local NVMe on GPU nodes with a disk-backed LRU. This reduces token-serving latency. Configure PID-based eviction thresholds at 70% and a background async flush to SAN for models > X MB or on deploy.
   - If SAN network becomes unavailable, Redwood should fallback to writing new model pushes to a local persistent PV (Retain policy) and queue async replication once SAN returns. This requires a small operator sidecar to manage replication state.

3) Persistence and retention policies
   - etcd: enable periodic snapshots to a dedicated PV on SAN; take snapshots every 15 minutes initially then tune.
   - Application PVs: models -> ReclaimPolicy: Retain; logs/metrics -> ReclaimPolicy: Delete with a TTL sidecar to push to your retention store.

4) Node pools & autoscaling
   - GPU nodepool: start with 4 nodes (A100) but configure cluster autoscaler with a max of 8. Tag GPU nodes with taints "dedicated=inference:NoSchedule".
   - Infra nodepool: 3 nodes for control plane & infra pods (metrics, logging) with anti-affinity across racks.
   - Storage nodepool (if you choose local replication): 3 dedicated OSD nodes per Rook/Ceph cluster (ideally 1 OSD per JBOD chassis across racks).

5) Network & egress controls
   - All workers use the customer NAT for egress. Redwood control-plane access will be via a fixed egress ACL (we will provide IPs).
   - We will require the following ports opened between racks: kube-apiserver (6443), etcd (2379/2380), and for Rook/Ceph: 6789, 6800-7300 (OSD range). Confirm if SAN paths require additional ports.

6) Operational items (delivery notes)
   - We will ship a small replication operator (sidecar) and a Vault KMS plugin to authenticate to your Vault endpoint.
   - We need a pre-staging window to snapshot models before the go-live and a 48-hour cutover runbook for final switch-over.

Action items (assigned):
   - Samir: confirm whether we can schedule the neutral tie-breaker VM or if you want snapshots to external S3 (air-gapped S3 gateway).
   - Neha: I'll need the SAN LUNs and FC/iSCSI target details to draft CSI manifest options.
   - Laura: please draft the runbook for the 48-hour cutover and I'll annotate storage failover steps.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
